title: Lists and spans
blurb: A list owns its elements and grows. A span is a view of memory someone else owns, and a string is a span of chars, with UTF-8 as library code you call when you need it.

title: Either types
blurb: `either` is the sum type. A variant can carry a payload or just a tag, and `opt` and `result` are two of them.

blocks.label: in core
blocks.code:
type opt[t] = either { none, some(t) }
type result[t, e] = either { ok(t), err(e) }

title: Optionals and results
blurb: `?t` is sugar for `opt[t]`. `?` is the else operator, and `.try` gives you the value or returns the error, on anything that implements `try`.

title: Control flow
blurb: `if` is an expression, `loop` breaks with a value, and `require` binds a pattern for the rest of the block or leaves.

title: Lambdas
blurb: A lambda captures only what you list in brackets. The physical form of the function depends on what you need: inlined, a direct call, an indirect call, or a dynamic closure.

blocks.label: program

title: Abilities
blurb: An ability is a set of functions a type can implement, sometimes called type classes or ad hoc polymorphism. It is the way to express a protocol without coupling your types to it. All of this compiles to plain function calls.

title: References
blurb: References are taken with `.&` and followed with `.*`. Every `*t` points at something, so there is nothing to null-check.

title: Early execution
blurb: Globals are computed while compiling, `#static` runs any expression there, and only the results reach the binary.
